title: Choose STLmill's visual world
question: The roll assigned Swatch Wall for the hub. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Swatch Wall
options.lineage: printed filament swatch cards hung on a workshop pegboard; shadow-board outlines for missing tools
options.thesis: Every generator hangs on the shop wall as a printed swatch card; empty hooks show the outline of what's coming.
options.viewport: A full-bleed pegboard. Top-left, the Clicker hangs as a large swatch card holding a live rotating 3D clicker; its text field is on the card and the model rebuilds as you type. The card's own tab, 'Open the mill', is the primary action. Beside it, three shadow-board outlines mark the tools to come, unlit. The wordmark is a small embossed swatch pinned top-left; the licence and tip note hang as a tag at the bottom.
options.risk: Reads as a themed illustration if the cards stop behaving like real UI; the hardboard ground must stay material, never drift to cream.

raised.raise: Reader is author: the hero card's text is editable in place and the 3D clicker rebuilds as you type.
Dimensions are fixed-position digit readouts; a size change is a visible physical tick, never a reflow.
Hierarchy by light: the live tool is lit and full-colour; future slots are unlit shadow outlines, never fake cards.
State reads on the whole material: hover lifts the entire card off its hook, no button-level chrome.
One pull propagates: the hub's single size slider re-deploys the whole demo clicker.

options.label: Parts Catalog
options.lineage: industrial mail-order parts catalog: line drawings, dimension callouts, ruled spec rows
options.thesis: Each generator is a catalog part: drawn, dimensioned, and ordered from one row.
options.viewport: A catalog spread: a narrow left index of tool categories, and the Clicker entry filling the page as a dimensioned line drawing (35 mm, 14 mm cutout, MX stem) with its spec table and a 'Configure' row as the action. Tools to come appear as catalog numbers marked 'not yet stocked'.
options.risk: The industrial-catalog look is where most maker brands land; strong, but recognisable at a glance.

options.label: Module Mosaic
options.thesis: The hub as a packed module mosaic: every tool, spec, and format on one screen.
options.viewport: A dense mosaic: the Clicker module with live preview top-left; spec modules (sizes, formats, switch fit, licence) tiled beside it; coming tools as ruled empty modules with orange tabs; a persistent multi-row nav rail. Utility red translates to brand orange.
options.case: Fuses well: spec density matches how makers evaluate a tool; loses on audience identification, reading as an e-commerce site rather than a workshop.
options.risk: Density without real content collapses into empty boxes; every module must be filled with true facts.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Tools as black-and-white cards you can paint and link yourself.
options.viewport: A stack of monochrome cards, each tool a painted button.
options.case: Fuses poorly: makers do not identify with 1980s desktop computing, and one-bit black-and-white erases the multi-colour printing story.
options.kept: Reader is author: the hero is editable in place.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Quantities as glowing orange digits in glass tubes.
options.viewport: Banks of glowing tubes counting metrics.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the hub has no counts to show and may not invent them; quantities-as-interface has nothing true to count.

options.label: Chromatophore Skin
options.lineage: cephalopod skin as a living display
options.thesis: The page surface changes pattern and texture with state.
options.viewport: A mantle-cream surface whose pattern travels under the cursor.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no connection to printing or hardware fit; GPU shader cost with no product payoff.
options.kept: State reads on the whole material, not on badges.

options.label: Miura Sheet
options.thesis: One pull unfolds the whole site from a hand-sized packet.
options.viewport: A gold packet that deploys into a tessellated sheet of tools.
options.case: Fuses only partly: deployment is a strong metaphor for a parametric tool, but makers do not read aerospace origami as their world and the fold grid fights legibility.

options.label: Signboard Alley
options.thesis: Tools stacked floor by floor as glowing signs on a wet street.
options.viewport: A building spine of lit signs, the ground floor loudest.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nightlife signage says nothing about printing; dark-and-neon is the look to avoid.
options.kept: Hierarchy by light: live tools lit, future ones unlit.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A generator hub as the category ships it: headline, subline, button, then a grid of tool cards with thumbnails.
canonCard.viewport: Centered headline over a subline and an orange button; below, a three-column card grid with a render thumbnail, name, one-line description, and 'Coming soon' badges.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other generator site, by design.
